study_identification_part.si_4_title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Three HCP Lifespan cohorts (HCP-D: Development, HCP-YA: Young Adult, HCP-A: Aging) were used for the healthy normative model. An additional single-site clinical dataset (MACC: Memory, Ageing & Cognition Centre, National University of Singapore) was used for clinical transfer evaluation. MACC is not a named dataset in the provided list, so it is categorized as SINGLE-SITE.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "This study uses three publicly available healthy brain imaging datasets that were provided and curated by the Human Connectome Project (HCP); namely, HCP's Young Adult, Aging, and Development cohorts." ... "we evaluated the model's translational capabilities to real-world data from memory clinics (Memory, Ageing & Cognition Centre at the National University of Singapore: MACC)"

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The three HCP datasets (HCP-D, HCP-YA, HCP-A) were pooled and stratified into 80% train (N=1978) and 20% test (N=495) splits for the normative model. The MACC clinical dataset was used for transfer learning: 66 healthy individuals from MACC were used to fine-tune site harmonization parameters, and the remaining MACC sample (HC, MCI, AD) was used to evaluate clinical normative deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Healthy individuals were stratified into train and test splits to enable validation of the fitted models on unseen data. Namely, 80% (Ntrain=1978 individuals) of the healthy data were used to train the model, and the remaining 20% (Ntest=495) were used for out-of-sample validation" ... "The normative model, pre-trained on Ntrain healthy individuals, was subsequently fine-tuned for the clinical sample of NMACC=674 individuals using transfer learning."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Mansour2025.pdf.md: Methods / 4.2 Train Test Split, L338; Methods / 4.5 Clinical Fine-tuning, L364

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using healthy individuals from three HCP cohorts (HCP-D: 652, HCP-YA: 1096, HCP-A: 725). These were split 80/20 into train (1978) and test (495). The overall-phase includes both train and test samples.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Overall-phase weighted mean was computed from per-cohort combined (train+test) values: HCP-D (N=652, 14.43+/-4.06), HCP-YA (N=1096, 28.79+/-3.69), HCP-A (N=725, 60.35+/-15.74). Train-phase weighted mean was computed from: HCP-D train (N=521, 14.41+/-4.06), HCP-YA train (N=877, 28.79+/-3.69), HCP-A train (N=580, 60.29+/-15.70). Pooled SDs computed as sqrt(sum((n_i-1)*sd_i^2)/sum(n_i-1)). Min/max from paper text: 'from 5 to 100 years old'. HCP-A ages above 90 were reported as 100 to protect health information. Train-phase min/max inferred from stratified splitting that preserved age distributions.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "These cohorts collectively comprised 2473 healthy individuals (54.7% female) spanning a wide age range, from 5 to 100 years old." Table S.1: HCP-D Train: 14.41 +/- 4.06, Test: 14.53 +/- 4.07; HCP-YA Train: 28.79 +/- 3.69, Test: 28.78 +/- 3.70; HCP-A Train: 60.29 +/- 15.70, Test: 60.61 +/- 15.89. "For all participants aged above 90 years old, age was reported as 100 to avoid releasing protected health information."
